items.title: Mean-surface and Codazzi characterizations of harmonic Lagrangian vector fields
items.difficulty_reason: The author first relates Lagrangian sections to divergence-free fields and scalar potentials, then computes the Lie derivative and vector Laplacian through the Hessian-minus-potential shape tensor. The proof uses harmonicity and Codazzi identities to derive constant trace and recovers the scalar equation by shifting the potential. These source-local computations and all three implications are retained as proof, not replaced by a citation. The equivalence is a structural ingredient of the separately selected boundary-extension uniqueness result.

compared.relation: Same paper; selected Theorem 6.1 gives uniqueness of extensions of circle vector fields under bounded antiholomorphic derivative. Theorem 4.6 characterizes all smooth harmonic Lagrangian fields via scalar mean surfaces and traceless Codazzi tensors. The latter is an explicitly shared proof dependency, not a second presentation of the uniqueness statement.
